rationale: A and C best communicate a complete, production-plausible paint-and-decal system: the pale aqua hull field, prominent charter branding, boat name, and separate artwork presentation create clear hierarchy and strong legibility. D and E remain clean and credible but provide less design detail and place the main identity in a somewhat tighter bow area. B looks natural on the water, yet its branding is too small and understated for an effective charter vessel. A narrowly leads C, while D narrowly leads E, because each pair appears visually indistinguishable at the supplied resolution.
uncertainty_notes: A/C and D/E appear effectively identical in the attachments, so ordering within those pairs is arbitrary. Low resolution limits assessment of small text, decal edges, exact colors, and real-world viewing distance; the incomplete brief may also omit required content or side-specific placement.
